=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.
exchanges.text:
## Overall assessment

The Seller’s package departs materially from Wattlebridge’s interests. Its central effect is to give the Seller broad protection for matters mentioned anywhere in the data room, while subjecting almost every potential claim—including title and potentially fraud—to the same restrictive remedies regime. It also leaves significant completion risks unresolved.

**Priority pushback:** protect clean title and the debt-free/cash-free bargain; make Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment and security release effective completion requirements; resolve the bonus and Ironquay exposures in the funds flow or through specific protection; and narrow the disclosure and liability limitations.

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note are not evidence that these positions are agreed. The assessment below is based on the supplied summary and Disclosure Letter, not the complete SPA or underlying DD documents; those documents and the current diligence record need to be checked before final drafting.

## 1. Liability, remedies and disclosure

### General warranty cap, thresholds and time limits

The proposed **20% cap (AUD 4.8 million)**, **AUD 25,000 de minimis**, excess-only **AUD 250,000 basket**, and **18-month notification period** all reduce recovery. The basket is a deductible: even after qualifying claims exceed AUD 250,000, the Buyer loses the first AUD 250,000. Related smaller losses may also fall out under the de minimis, depending on how “claim” is defined.

**Push back:** Seek a higher general cap, lower thresholds, a tipping basket under which the whole qualifying amount is recoverable once the basket is crossed, aggregation of related claims for the de minimis, and a longer notification period. Ensure a properly notified claim survives expiry long enough to investigate and pursue it. The appropriate final numbers are commercial negotiation points, not established by the supplied materials.

### Fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities

Applying the general cap and 18-month limit to **capacity and title** is particularly problematic: the Buyer could pay AUD 24 million yet have only AUD 4.8 million of recourse if it does not receive what it bought. Tax and identified liabilities can also emerge after 18 months or exceed general warranty thresholds.

**Push back:**

- Give title, ownership, authority and capacity warranties a separate cap of at least the purchase price, longer survival, and no general de minimis or basket.
- Seek a separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-completion tax, with a longer period aligned to relevant assessment periods, a suitable cap and no general thresholds.
- Keep negotiated specific indemnities outside the general warranty cap, basket, de minimis and short time limit, with appropriately tailored limits and survival.
- Require express carve-outs for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation by the relevant Seller persons. Review the drafting under NSW law rather than assuming a broad exclusion will be ineffective.

### “All Claims,” exclusive remedies and non-reliance

The proposal that limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature** is much wider than a general warranty regime. Depending on the full definitions, it may impair claims under the tax covenant, specific indemnities, completion obligations and other remedies, including claims arising from deliberate misconduct.

**Push back:** Map each limitation to the specific categories of claim it is intended to govern. Expressly preserve the agreed treatment of fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, completion obligations and fraud, as well as rights needed to enforce completion and obtain appropriate equitable relief. Review clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 together with their definitions; do not rely on labels alone.

### Blanket disclosure and Buyer knowledge

The Seller purports to disclose everything in the data room and public records, and to bar claims for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew **or could have discovered**. This could transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer without the Seller clearly explaining their nature and effect.

**Push back:** Permit disclosure against warranties only where a matter is **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope**, by specific reference to accessible materials supplied before an agreed cut-off. Reject blanket data-room and public-register disclosure and “discoverable” knowledge. If a knowledge qualification is unavoidable, confine it to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without imputed adviser knowledge or a duty to search. Specific indemnities, price adjustments and completion obligations should not be defeated simply because a matter was disclosed or known.

## 2. Completion and deal economics

### Bluefen consent — significant customer concentration

Bluefen represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million or 30% of FY26 revenue**. DD-002 records a change-control consent and associated conditions, but the Seller has supplied neither final written consent nor evidence that those conditions are met. A reasonable-endeavours obligation and a clause deeming consent satisfied on receipt of a letter may leave the Buyer with a purported consent that is conditional, ineffective or commercially adverse.

**Push back:** Make an effective written consent, on terms acceptable to the Buyer, and satisfaction or valid waiver of all associated conditions a condition to completion. Require delivery and verification before completion, with a long-stop and suitable termination rights if it is not obtained. Check the actual contract and consent for adverse amendments, fees or continuing conditions; do not assume consent has been obtained.

### Riverlark — debt and security at completion

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** remains outstanding, and no final security discharge is included. A release promised after completion conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free baseline and exposes the Buyer to both repayment and residual security risk.

**Push back:** Require an agreed payoff amount and irrevocable payout and release arrangements before completion, with repayment directly from completion proceeds and effective release of relevant guarantees and security at or immediately through completion. Include undertakings and evidence for any registrations that must be discharged subsequently. Ensure debt is deducted in the price/funds-flow mechanics, with no double recovery, and no reliance on an unsecured post-completion promise.

### Completion bonuses and supplier renewals

The **AUD 420,000 bonuses** are conditional on completion and continued employment and are absent from the funds flow. The record does not establish applicable payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. Even if payable after completion, they could become Company liabilities attributable to the sale.

**Push back:** Determine who bears the bonuses and on-costs, identify the beneficiaries and conditions, and require a Seller-funded payment or an explicit debt-like/transaction-expense adjustment in the completion accounts and funds flow. Avoid double counting.

The **three Sandbar renewals total AUD 330,000**. Their timing and treatment are unresolved; the documents do not establish that all are ordinary-course, unavoidable, accrued or terminable.

**Push back:** Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and obtain the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and accrual status. Allocate any pre-completion accruals or committed transaction-related costs consistently with the agreed price mechanism; do not automatically deduct the whole amount without establishing its nature.

## 3. Identified legal and operational risks

### Ironquay IP

Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditioned on cleared payment of **every SOW3 fee**. DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently prove non-payment; there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. A payment-only indemnity may compensate for a fee but leave the Company without usable or transferable IP.

**Push back:** Verify all SOW3 fees and obtain evidence of cleared payment, a direct confirmation or assignment of all relevant rights, and any necessary licence or waiver before completion. Broaden the specific indemnity to cover resulting third-party claims, remediation and losses from defective ownership or use rights, not just the stated payment. Confirm that it sits outside general warranty limitations.

### Export/privacy incident

DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address, potentially involving **approximately 1,240 records**. Access, scope and notification requirements remain unknown; this is **not established as a confirmed breach** and no loss has been quantified. Its uncertainty is a reason for investigation, not dismissal.

**Push back:** Require prompt forensic investigation and preservation of evidence, access logs, containment and a documented assessment of applicable contractual and legal notification obligations. Obtain updates before completion and consider a tailored indemnity or other protection for pre-completion causes and related investigation, notification and remediation costs. Determine whether completion protection or a condition is warranted once the facts are clearer.

### Title verification

DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the issued shares, but the Buyer has not independently verified title. A register alone does not resolve all issues concerning issuance, encumbrances, options or transfer restrictions.

**Push back:** Verify the register against corporate records, constitution, share issuances and any options or security arrangements. Require delivery of effective transfers and share certificates where applicable, release of encumbrances, appropriate corporate approvals, and robust fundamental title warranties.

### Lease and Mossvale

DD-007 identifies a **lease notification**, not a stated landlord consent requirement. DD-009 contains an **assignment restriction**, not a stated share-sale consent requirement. A share purchase does not itself establish an assignment.

**Recommendation:** Check the complete provisions and related documents, ensure any required notice is delivered on time, and confirm whether any wider change-control or indirect-transfer language applies. Do not demand consents on the current record merely because an assignment restriction exists.

## Recommended negotiation sequence

1. **Completion blockers:** Bluefen consent and conditions; Riverlark payoff and releases; clean share title; verified Ironquay rights.
2. **Protect the economics:** Build debt, bonuses and applicable on-costs into an agreed, internally consistent completion funds flow and price-adjustment mechanism; investigate the supplier renewals.
3. **Repair the risk allocation:** Narrow disclosure and knowledge provisions; separate fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity regimes; revise general cap, basket and time limits; preserve fraud and enforcement remedies.
4. **Resolve incident uncertainty:** Obtain an investigation and notification assessment promptly, then tailor protection to the evidence.
5. **Check the complete documents:** Confirm definitions, conditions, notice procedures, interaction of remedies and all relevant DD provisions before settling drafting.
